newsitem.title: USA: Corporate Express acquires supply units. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Corporate Express acquires supply units. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]

text.p: Corporate Express Inc, a supplier of office products and services to large corporations, said it had made a string of acquisitions of companies (corrects from "stores") in the same industry in Canada, Europe and the United States.
The company said in a statement it had also signed letters of intent to make more acquisitions throughout the world.
It said it had made acquisitions in Canada, France, Germany, the United Kingdom and the United States.

Without revealing the terms of the deals, it said it had bought France's Harvard Information Support and 26 Avenue; British Abraxas Computer Supplies; as well as Messerknecht Burokommunikation GmbH and BIT Buro und Informationstechnik GmbH in Germany.
The company also said it had acquired Canada's Intergroup Business Products and Johnson Office Products, and 15 office supply companies (corrects from "stores") throughout the United States.
Corporate Express said the acquisitions had combined revenue totalling about $270 million.

It said it had definitive agreements or letters of intent with acquisition candidates around the world with revenue totalling more than $500 million, including $280 million from the previously announced merger with United TransNet, Inc.
Corporate Express operates in more than 500 locations, including 100 distribution centers.
It employs more than 14,000 people in the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Germany, France and the United Kingdom.
